Distinguished from Sara Adler (stepmother) by being the Dinah Feinman line.

distinguishing: Julius Adler (b. 15 Nov 1880 Bialystok; family name really Adler, also called 'Ortshik'), choirmaster-conductor-actor turned director-impresario in Poland (Lodz: Sokolo Theatre with Sierotzki, Grosser Teater) and later Riga (Nayer yidisher teater 1928-29). Alternated between Poland/Russia and America (1904-09, 1920-27). Playwright/translator of operettas and dramas; husband (per Emilia's entry) of actress Emilia Adler; not connected to the Jacob P. Adler dynasty by the entry.

distinguishing: Jacob P. Adler (1855 Odessa - 31 March 1926 New York), the most famous star of the American Yiddish stage: a lead actor, theatre owner/manager and Gordin's chief interpreter, famous for Uriel Acosta, David Moshele in The Jewish King Lear, Shylock, and Ben-Tsion. He began with Goldfaden/Rosenberg troupes in Russia in 1879, moved to London in 1882 and to New York in 1890, and ran the Pulis, People's, Grand and Thalia theatres in New York. His wives were Sophie Oberlender and later Sara, and his daughters were Frances and Julia. He wrote the memoirs 'Mayn lebens bashraybung' / '40 yohr oyf der bihne'. He should not be confused with the London chief rabbi Dr. Adler, who is mentioned in this entry as his patron.

distinguishing: Sam Adler (b. c.1868 Zvenigorodka, d. Vienna 26 Nov 1925), a reclusive pioneer who returned from America to Russia in 1900 and ran his own well-organized troupe 'Sem Adler of America' (also Yiddish-German troupe) touring the Pale and Petersburg/Kiev; famous for staging reforms (salaried actors, discipline, clean language) and teacher of Ben-Ami, Lazar Fried, Esther Rokhl Kaminska-type actors. Ended in poverty in Vienna; no family mentioned. Earlier than the Jacob P. Adler / Julius Adler generation; a director-manager, comic, not related by stated family ties.
